A ✓ status covers only the recomputed numerical checks; it is not design acceptance. The equation notes of the calculation are in its report.

report.paragraph: Inputs are highlighted amber; results are the green tables.
Overview

Clearance between the end-bent piles and the MSE wall facing so that the soil-reinforcement straps clear the piles. The front wall needs the calculated minimum clear for a strap of the trial width at the selected skew; the side walls need the specified 24-in pile-face clear. Both are compared with the wall lines of the CAD model at each pile of both end bents, using the nominal pile width without a placement envelope.

In the CAD model the side walls stand at the 24-in criterion within 0.0002 in, so the side-wall rows read MEETS CLEAR or SHORTFALL only by the last digits of the model coordinates. The 24-in setback from the front cap face to the back of the front facing is a separate check.
Outside this calculation: the strap design itself (Specialty Engineer), the cheek webs outside the cap ends, and the wall facing design.
Overview and result summary
Both end bents | 19 October 2026 (first issued 13 October 2026) | Front strap check; specified side offsets

Evaluate a straight strap from the FRONT wall on the normal through a nominal pile center. Use the selected alpha in either skew direction. The SIDE walls use a separate specified 24-inch minimum; their strap routing is not evaluated.

5. Separate requirements and use

textcell.name: CapSetbackR1C0
textcell.paragraph: Front cap face to back of front facing

report.paragraph: Front strap clearance and cap-to-facing clearance are separate measurements. Keep the front face of the cap at least 24 inches from the back of facing. The cap is shown in plan for coordination; no elevation strap/cap clearance is solved here.

The side-wall 24-inch pile-face offset is the specified layout criterion for this check. SDG 3.13.2.N.2.i applies 24 inches to cap/front-facing clearance; N.2.ii applies it to battered pile/leveling-pad clearance. Those provisions are not a side-wall strap-clearance calculation.

Pile placement tolerance is excluded as requested. Skew may be reversed around the nominal pile, but this does not demonstrate clearance for all possible as-built positions or the full reinforcement route. Coordinate actual pile positions and adjacent obstructions separately.

Only the front wall is checked for nominal centered-strap geometry. Side reinforcement, rear walls, elevation routing, reinforcement length, connection/development and wall stability are outside this module. No side or overall wall-design pass is implied.

The plan assumes wall faces parallel to these axes. Nominal pile width defines the clearance; the tiny saved frame rotation is retained for pile centers and the cap outline. The open boundary has no rear edge or rear-wall requirement.
FDOT Structures Manual, January 2026 — SDG 3.13.2.K.8 and N.2.
